info.name: Keyframe
info.description:
Keyframe v0.1.0 (ALPHA) REST API: summaries and typed metadata from images, video, and audio (audio is heard by a listening model, not only transcribed), audio measurements and sections, segment retrieval, and analytics.

Set the collection variables before sending: protocol, host, and port build baseUrl; accessKey is sent as x-api-key on every request; adminKey is used by admin-only requests (settings, restart, endpoint tests, request history deletion, analytics). sampleImageUrl, sampleVideoUrl, sampleAudioUrl, sampleMusicUrl, and sampleSectionsUrl must be publicly reachable, because the server refuses private-network URLs by default. listeningEndpoint names the endpoint the Listen requests use (llama-listen on the factory configuration).

Run order that exercises everything: System, Image, Video / Analyze video (job), Audio / Analyze audio (job), Jobs / Get job until Succeeded, Jobs / Get job result, Segments, then Endpoints, Analytics, Settings, and Request History. Full reference: REST_API.md in the repository.

variable.description: Built from protocol, host, and port
Admin key (Auth.AdminApiKey). Change it on any shared server.
Publicly reachable audio URL (mp3, wav, flac, m4a, ogg, or webm)
Base64 image bytes for the inline example
Set by the Video folder test scripts
Set by Get settings; sent by Update settings
Set by Analytics / List analyses and Audio / Analyze audio (wait, defaults)
Listening endpoint for the Listen requests. Alternatives: vllm-voxtral (listen-gpu profile, activate it first) or any Gemini or OpenAI-compatible endpoint you add.
Music for the listening requests: Josh Woodward, "Ships" (CC BY 4.0, 2:02), long enough that a 120-second listen budget (llama-listen) hears excerpts
Recording with silences for the Sections request: the factory sample, three spoken clips separated by 4-second silences (89 s)

item.name: System
item.description: Liveness, health, and identity. Health and the root page are anonymous so orchestrators and load balancers can probe them without a key.

request.description: Liveness check. Returns 200 with no body. Anonymous.
Small HTML page with the version and links to the API documentation. Anonymous.
Version, uptime, ffmpeg availability, database provider, job counts, and endpoint health. Status is Degraded when ffmpeg is missing. Anonymous.
Resolves the presented key: principal name, whether it is the admin key, and whether the server requires authentication. Returns 401 without a valid key.
The OpenAPI 3 document generated from the server's route metadata. Anonymous.

item.name: Image
item.description: Synchronous image analysis. Supply the image by Url or base64 Data. Every Context item is included in every prompt the request produces. The response carries Results (keyed the way you asked), per-field detail in Fields, media Properties, and Telemetry with stage timings, every model call, and token counts.

request.description: Summary plus four typed fields from an image URL, with a Context list. Private-network URLs are refused unless Media.AllowPrivateNetworkUrls is true.
Same request with inline base64 data and PerField mode, which makes one model call per field. Replace {{sampleImageBase64}} with base64 image bytes (for example: base64 -i photo.jpg).
Selects a configured endpoint by name and overrides its model. An unknown endpoint name returns 400.
Deterministic media properties from ffprobe: dimensions, duration, codecs, tags. No model calls.

item.name: Video
item.description: Video analysis runs as a background job. The response is 202 with the job unless Wait is true and the job finishes within WaitTimeoutMs, in which case it is 200 with the full result. The test scripts store the job id in the jobId collection variable for the Jobs folder.

request.description: Queues a job with scenes, per-scene captions and fields, a transcript, and whole-video summary and fields. Poll Jobs / Get job, then Jobs / Get job result.

exec: pm.test('job accepted or finished', function () { pm.expect([200, 202]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Waits up to WaitTimeoutMs (capped by Jobs.MaxWaitTimeoutMs) and returns the result inline when the job succeeds in time. A job that finishes without succeeding returns 200 with the job so you can read Status and Error.

exec: pm.test('job accepted or finished', function () { pm.expect([200, 202]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: With TextModel set, the whole-video summary and fields are produced by a text-only model from the scene results and transcript instead of from frames.

exec: pm.test('job accepted or finished', function () { pm.expect([200, 202]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Each scene's audio is attached to that scene's model calls when the vision endpoint accepts audio (Gemini or an OpenAI-compatible server). The default Ollama vision endpoints do not, so on the factory stack Listening reports EndpointLacksAudioInput and scenes use frames and transcript, as saved in the example. Scene audio never causes a 400.

response.name: Ollama vision endpoint (no audio input)

originalRequest.description: Each scene's audio is attached to that scene's model calls when the vision endpoint accepts audio (Gemini or an OpenAI-compatible server). The default Ollama vision endpoints do not, so on the factory stack Listening reports EndpointLacksAudioInput and scenes use frames and transcript, as saved in the example. Scene audio never causes a 400.

item.name: Audio
item.description: Audio analysis runs as a background job, like video: 202 with the job (MediaKind Audio), or 200 with the full AudioAnalysisResponse when Wait is true and the job finishes in time. Accepts audio files (mp3, wav, flac, m4a or aac, ogg or opus, webm audio) and video files (audio track only). Transcribe, Summarize, Listen, and Measure are on by default. The listening model hears the audio itself, not only the transcript; without a usable audio-capable endpoint the analysis falls back to the transcript and Listening.Listened is false with a reason code. The test scripts store the job id in jobId for the Jobs folder and the analysis id in analysisId for the Analytics folder.

request.description: Queues a job that transcribes the recording with the whisper endpoint, then summarizes it and extracts fields with the text model. Poll Jobs / Get job, then Jobs / Get job result.

exec: pm.test('job accepted or finished', function () { pm.expect([200, 202]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Only the source and Wait: the defaults transcribe and summarize. Returns 200 with the AudioAnalysisResponse (Transcript, Results.Summary, Telemetry) when the job finishes within WaitTimeoutMs.

item.name: Analyze audio track of a video

request.description: A video file as the source: only its audio track is transcribed, no frames are extracted, and the response carries a warning.

exec: pm.test('job accepted or finished', function () { pm.expect([200, 202]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: The listening model hears the audio itself, with the transcript as a hint, so questions about how the recording sounds (live or studio, instruments) are answered from the sound. The factory configuration listens through a llama-server on the host at port 8720, reached from the containers as llama-listen (start one with: llama-server -hf ggml-org/Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-GGUF:Q4_K_M --port 8720), or through the keyframe-llama container with docker compose --profile listen. A recording longer than the endpoint's listen budget (120 seconds on llama-listen) is heard as evenly spaced excerpts, and Listening says so. When the listening server is stopped or still loading, the request still succeeds from the transcript and Listening.Listened is false with reason EndpointUnhealthy; both outcomes are saved as examples. Check Listening.Listened before trusting an answer about how the audio sounds.

response.name: Listened (excerpts on llama-server)

request.description: The same listening request served by vLLM running Voxtral Mini 3B. Start it with docker compose --profile listen-gpu up -d on a host with an NVIDIA GPU (about 10 GB of free GPU memory), then activate the vllm-voxtral endpoint on the Settings page (it ships inactive). The default listen budget of 1200 seconds hears a typical track whole (Mode Full).

request.description: Splits the recording at silences (ffmpeg silencedetect; models never choose boundaries) and summarizes each section by listening to it. With TextModel set, the whole-recording summary is reduced from the section results with the text model (Listening.Mode Sections). sampleSectionsUrl points at the factory sample, three spoken clips separated by 4-second silences, so it yields three sections. A section longer than the listen budget is heard as a centered excerpt. Each section can be cut back out with POST /v1.0/segment. Runs as a job; poll it from the Jobs folder.

response.name: Sections (job result)

originalRequest.description: Splits the recording at silences (ffmpeg silencedetect; models never choose boundaries) and summarizes each section by listening to it. With TextModel set, the whole-recording summary is reduced from the section results with the text model (Listening.Mode Sections). A section longer than the listen budget is heard as a centered excerpt. Each section can be cut back out with POST /v1.0/segment. Runs as a job; poll it from the Jobs folder.

request.description: When a recording is longer than the listen budget and sections are off, the model hears SampleClips evenly spaced excerpts of ClipSeconds each in one call, each labeled with its offset. When SampleClips times ClipSeconds exceeds the budget, the excerpts are shortened and a warning says so.

item.name: Segments
item.description: Cut a time range out of a video or audio source: a video clip (Output Video, mp4 or webm), an audio clip (Output Audio, mp3, wav, flac, m4a, or ogg), or a still frame at StartMs (Output Frame, jpg or png). Use StartMs and EndMs from Scenes or Transcript.Segments of an analysis result and resend the same Source; Keyframe does not keep uploaded media. Binary responses carry Content-Disposition and x-keyframe-segment-start-ms, -end-ms, and -duration-ms headers. Use Send and Download in Postman to save the media.

request.description: A re-encoded mp4 clip of 1000 to 3500 ms, scaled to 480 pixels on the long edge. EndMs past the end of the media is clamped.
The audio of the same range as mp3. Works on video and audio sources; a source without an audio track is 422.
A JPEG still at StartMs returned as a SegmentResponse with base64 Data. EndMs is ignored for frames.
EndMs before StartMs and an audio format for video output: 400 with every problem in Details.

item.name: Jobs
item.description: Durable background jobs. Status is Queued, Running, Succeeded, Failed, Canceled, or Interrupted (the server stopped mid-job). Finished jobs are pruned after Jobs.RetentionDays.

Cancels a queued or running job. Returns 409 when the job already finished.
Deletes a finished job and its result. Returns 409 for a queued or running job.

item.name: Analytics
item.description: Every finished image, video, and audio analysis is stored as an analysis row plus one row per model call attempt. These requests read and delete them, and all use the admin key. Summary distributions report Count, Min, Max, Avg, P50, P90, P95, P99, StdDev, and Sum; every bucket in the range is present. Analytics.Enable and Analytics.RetentionDays control writing and pruning.

item.name: Settings
item.description: Admin only. Secrets come back masked as **** plus their last four characters; send them back unchanged to keep them. Fields metadata marks each setting Live or Restart.

request.description: Masked settings, per-field metadata, RestartRequired, and the settings file path.

Responds 202, then exits so the container runtime relaunches the server and reloads settings. Outside a supervisor the server simply stops.
